cues.en: You're listening to Do the Internet Better. One take, five minutes, live in the SquareWeave studio.
cues.zh: 你在收听《让互联网更好》。一次录制，五分钟，SquareWeave 演播室现场直播。

cues.en: Hi.
cues.zh: 嗨。

cues.en: My name's Will. I'm hoping that today I'll get you excited about user interface and user experience design using a method that we call the user is drunk.
cues.zh: 我叫 Will。希望今天能通过一种我们称为“用户是醉汉”的方法，让你对用户界面和用户体验设计产生兴趣。

cues.en: But to talk about interfaces, we first have to ask what is an interface?
cues.zh: 但要说界面，我们首先得问：什么是界面？

cues.en: People say it's a keyboard, or it's a bunch of buttons on a screen.
cues.zh: 人们会说它是键盘，或者屏幕上的一堆按钮。

cues.en: Realistically,
cues.zh: 实际上，

cues.en: an interface is where two things meet. It's the interface in language between accountancy and law. It could be the interface
cues.zh: 界面是两样东西相接的地方。它是会计与法律在语言上的交界。它也可以是

cues.en: between air and water. Surface tension is an interface.
cues.zh: 空气与水之间的交界。表面张力就是一种界面。

cues.en: And when you realize that interfaces are real things, you start to realize that a lot of the stuff on the web is just echoes of real life.
cues.zh: 当你意识到界面是真实存在的东西，就会发现网上很多东西其实只是现实生活的映射。

cues.en: For instance, a door that has a round handle is much harder to turn than a door that has a lever handle. A door that opens for you automatically
cues.zh: 比如，圆形门把手比杠杆式门把手难拧得多。自动为你打开的门

cues.en: is like a login form that remembers who you are. A twist top bottle is a lot easier to open than a bottle that requires a bottle opener.
cues.zh: 就像记得你是谁的登录表单。旋盖瓶比需要开瓶器的瓶子好开得多。

cues.en: You've seen tabs,
cues.zh: 大家见过标签页、

cues.en: breadcrumbs,
cues.zh: 面包屑导航，

cues.en: and even radio buttons that are all real life things that we've transferred into the Internet.
cues.zh: 甚至是单选框，这些都是我们搬到互联网上的现实事物。

cues.en: One of the beautiful things about great UI is that it's not there.
cues.zh: 优秀的 UI 有个奇妙之处：它让人感觉不到它的存在。

cues.en: It's like lovers who talk without talking. It's like a guitar player who just
cues.zh: 就像心有灵犀的恋人无需多言；就像吉他手弹奏时，

cues.en: lets the music come out and they're not really sure if the guitar's there anymore.
cues.zh: 只是任由音乐流淌，甚至察觉不到吉他的存在。

cues.en: If you can make your user interfaces porous so that people don't realize they're there, they will use them much more effectively.
cues.zh: 如果你能让用户界面变得如此通透，让人浑然不觉，用户的使用效率就会高得多。

cues.en: For example, the amount of embarrassing things that are said on Facebook through Facebook chat is because people can use them while they're actually blind drunk. It's because the UI is that good.
cues.zh: 比如，Facebook 聊天里说了多少尴尬的话，就是因为人们可以在烂醉如泥时还能用。因为 UI 就是那么好用。

cues.en: So let's look at what makes a drunk a drunk.
cues.zh: 那我们来瞧瞧是什么让醉汉成为醉汉。

cues.en: They've got blurry vision,
cues.zh: 他们视线模糊，

cues.en: which means that you should be able to understand what a site is doing when it's blurry
cues.zh: 这意味着你应该能在模糊的时候也明白网站是干什么的

cues.en: as when it's not. Guess what the big blue button does? It does the thing the site's there for.
cues.zh: 跟不模糊时一样。猜猜那个大蓝按钮是干嘛的？它就是这网站存在的目的。

cues.en: They're really attention poor. It's like, I'm gonna get a Souvlaki, then we're gonna go dancing, then we're gonna go drinking. I... How do you deal with that? You guide them through the process. It's kinda like, okay, put on your shoes. Now we're gonna get into the taxi.
cues.zh: 他们的注意力真的很差。就像是：“我要去吃烤肉串，然后去跳舞，再去喝酒。”我……这要怎么应付？你得一步一步引导他们。比如：“好，穿上鞋。现在我们去坐出租车。”

cues.en: Now we're gonna go to the club. Or, okay, you've bought your ticket. Now you need to download your ticket. Now you need to... Etcetera, etcetera. Guide them through a process as though they're blind drunk, and you'll actually get a real approximation of what an average user is like.
cues.zh: 现在我们要去俱乐部。或者：“好，你已经买好票了。现在要下载票。接下来你得……如此等等。”像引导一个醉得不省人事的人那样，带他们一步步完成流程，你就能真正模拟出普通用户的样子。

cues.en: If in any doubt, say it twice. You are about to delete an item.
cues.zh: 只要有任何不确定，就重复确认一次。比如“你即将删除一个项目”。

cues.en: Congratulations,
cues.zh: 以及“恭喜，

cues.en: you have deleted the item.
cues.zh: 你已删除该项目”。

cues.en: Say it twice.
cues.zh: 重要的事情说两遍。

cues.en: A really good example of this is speed signs.
cues.zh: 限速标志就是个绝佳的例子。

cues.en: In all Australian law, in all of our roads, there's a 60 k speed sign, and then like another couple of 100 meters later, there's another 60 k speed sign. It's because you don't realize it the first time, but you see it twice, and you go, oh, okay, and then you slow down again. So say everything twice, confirmation dialogues,
cues.zh: 根据澳大利亚法律，在我们所有的道路上，先有一个 60 码的限速牌，接着开出两三百米，又会出现一个 60 码的牌子。这是因为你第一次可能没注意到，但连看两次就会意识到并慢下来。所以凡事确认两次，比如加个确认对话框，

cues.en: even just a little effect that proves that they've actually done something.
cues.zh: 或者哪怕只是个微动效，来证明操作确实生效了。

cues.en: Emotion really, really matters. Drunk people go from best friends to 50 cups in seconds. On the web, it's even worse because people will go from annoyed at your site to closing it with a click of a button. A great way around this is over the shoulder testing.
cues.zh: 情绪真的非常非常重要。醉酒的人几秒钟内就能从最好的朋友变成喝了50杯。在网络上，情况更糟，因为人们会从对你的网站有点烦，到一点按钮就把它关掉。一个很好的解决办法是肩并肩测试。

cues.en: Put somebody on a laptop in a real room and ask them to do some stuff. Please log in. Please download the form. Do whatever it is and just watch them You'll see the drunken master arise. They'll start to click on things frantically, their brow will furrow, and they'll get really, really emotional, and that's where you see the problems.
cues.zh: 让某人坐在真实房间里的笔记本电脑前，请他们做一些事情。请登录。请下载表格。做该做的事，然后仔细观察他们，你会看到“醉拳大师”现身。他们会开始疯狂点击，眉头紧锁，情绪变得非常非常激动，问题正是在这里暴露出来的。

cues.en: One important thing about the drunk is that he is not an idiot. A person with an IQ of 160
cues.zh: 关于醉酒用户，有件事很重要：他们并不傻。一个智商 160 的人

cues.en: who's drunk still has an IQ of 160. They just get more pedantic and more annoyed.
cues.zh: 喝醉了，智商也还是 160。只不过会更爱较真，也更容易不耐烦。

cues.en: So don't talk down to them. Don't be overly simplistic in what you do. And if they're a power user, let them be a power user.
cues.zh: 所以别居高临下地跟他们说话，也别把你做的东西设计得过于简单。如果他们是高级用户，就让他们按高级用户的方式使用。

cues.en: Because realistically,
cues.zh: 因为说实话，

cues.en: the user is not actually drunk, the user is fine.
cues.zh: 用户其实没醉，用户好得很。

cues.en: But with the amount of attention after dealing with Bob with accounts,
cues.zh: 可处理完 Bob 的账户问题，

cues.en: Jennifer and HR who I really want to sleep with, the kids, the wife, the family, soccer, my gun practice in the afternoon, the amount of time left to pay attention to UUI, which you love and I could not give a shit about, is
cues.zh: 再加上 Jennifer 和人力资源部——我真想跟 Jennifer 睡一觉，还有孩子、妻子、家人、足球，以及下午的射击练习，留给 UUI 的注意力少得可怜。你很喜欢 UUI，可我一点也不在乎。

cues.en: nothing. Nothing at all. So should you test this? Should you go home, drink a martini, and go through your application?
cues.zh: 一点都没有。所以你该测试这个吗？你该回家喝杯马提尼，再把你的应用从头到尾过一遍吗？

cues.en: Definitely not. It's really, really unconstructive.
cues.zh: 绝对不是。这真的非常、非常没有建设性。
